\begin{theorem}[Halting persists for longer choice words]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.halted_of_le}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.halted_of_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $K$ work tapes and Boolean symbols,
let $C$ be a configuration on a fixed Boolean input, and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. If every
choice word of length exactly $n$ takes $M$ from $C$ to a halting configuration, then
every choice word of length at least $n$ also takes $M$ from $C$ to a halting
configuration.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Randomized.Amplify.bump_val}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.bump_val}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.bump}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $c<r+2$ satisfy $c\le r$, and let $b$ be a Boolean. Increasing
$c$ by one when $b$ is true and leaving it unchanged when $b$ is false gives the value
$c+1$ if $b$ is true and $c$ if $b$ is false.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Machine acceptance]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.acc}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.acc}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, input string $x$, and choice string
$l$, define the acceptance bit to be true exactly when the output produced by running
$N$ on $x$ with choices $l$ is the one-symbol string consisting of true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Amplified decision value]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.val}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.val}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.acc, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.randProb, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, a Boolean input $x$, a natural number
$T$ of steps, a function $d:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, natural
numbers $i,c$, and $v\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, define the value to be the
probability that applying $d$ to $c$ plus the number of accepting blocks among $i$
blocks of length $T$ yields $v$, when the random choice string has length $iT$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-block acceptance value]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.val_zero}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.val_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.val, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_const}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean
input, and let $T,c$ be natural numbers and $v$ a Boolean. With zero blocks, the
acceptance value at offset $c$ is $1$ if the decision function sends $c$ to $v$, and is
$0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-block recurrence for acceptance value]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.val_succ}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.val_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.acc, Randomized.Amplify.val, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.blockCount_succ, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_bool_false, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_or_disjoint, Randomized.randProb_split}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean
input, let $T,i,c$ be natural numbers, and let $v$ be a Boolean. Write $p$ for the
fraction of length-$T$ choice strings on which $N$ outputs exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
Then the fraction of length-$(i+1)T$ choice strings for which the decision function
applied to $c$ plus the number of accepting blocks among the first $i+1$ blocks equals
$v$ is $p$ times the corresponding fraction for $i$ blocks with offset $c+1$, plus
$(1-p)$ times that fraction with offset $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting after an amplified run]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.run_halts}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.run_halts}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.ACfg, Randomized.Amplify.Fresh, Randomized.Amplify.RewindAt, Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.emb, Randomized.Amplify.halts_comp, Randomized.Amplify.rewindAt_emb, Randomized.Amplify.step_emb, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on Boolean inputs, let $r,T,m$
be natural numbers, and let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. Suppose every choice
word of length $T$ makes $N$ halt on input $x$. For a run index $j\in\{0,\ldots,r\}$,
counter $c\in\{0,\ldots,r+1\}$, and configuration $D$ of the amplified machine, suppose
every work-tape block with index greater than $j$ is blank with its head at $0$. Also
suppose that, from every configuration in the rewind phase for run $j$, every choice
word of length $m$ makes the amplified machine halt. Then every choice word of length
$T+m$, started from the embedding of $N$’s initial configuration at run $j$ and counter
$c$ into $D$, makes the amplified machine halt.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output probability in the amplified run]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.run_prob}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.run_prob}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.ACfg, Randomized.Amplify.Fresh, Randomized.Amplify.RewindAt, Randomized.Amplify.acc, Randomized.Amplify.accBit, Randomized.Amplify.accBit_runWith, Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.bump_val, Randomized.Amplify.emb, Randomized.Amplify.randProb_comp, Randomized.Amplify.rewindAt_emb, Randomized.Amplify.step_emb, Randomized.Amplify.val, Randomized.Amplify.val_succ, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_bool_false, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on Boolean inputs, with input
$x$, and let $r,T$ be natural numbers. Suppose every choice word of length $T$ makes $N$
halt on $x$. Choose $v\in\{0,1\}$, a natural number $i$, a run index
$j\in\{0,\ldots,r\}$ with $j+i=r$, a counter $c\in\{0,\ldots,r+1\}$ with $c\le j$, and
an amplified-machine configuration $D$ whose work-tape blocks with index greater than
$j$ are blank with their heads at $0$. Let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. Assume
every choice word of length $i(T+|x|+2)+1$ halts the amplified machine from any rewind
configuration for run $j$. Also assume that, for every such rewind configuration with
counter $c'\le j+1$, the probability that a uniformly random choice word of that length
produces output $[v]$ equals the probability that $\mathrm{dec}(c'+s)=v$, where $s$
counts the $T$-bit blocks among $i$ blocks accepted by $N$ on $x$ in a uniformly random
$iT$-bit word. Then the probability that a uniformly random choice word of length
$T+i(T+|x|+2)+1$, started from the embedding of $N$’s initial configuration at run $j$
and counter $c$, produces output $[v]$ equals the probability that
$\mathrm{dec}(c+s')=v$, where $s'$ counts the accepted $T$-bit blocks among $i+1$ blocks
in a uniformly random $(i+1)T$-bit word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting during rewind]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.rewind_halts}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.rewind_halts}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.ACfg, Randomized.Amplify.Fresh, Randomized.Amplify.RewindAt, Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.halted_of_le, Randomized.Amplify.restart, Randomized.Amplify.restart_eq_emb, Randomized.Amplify.rewind_last, Randomized.Amplify.rewind_run, Randomized.Amplify.run_halts, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean inputs, let $x$ be an
input, and let $r,T$ be natural numbers. Suppose every choice word of length exactly
$T$, run on $N$ from its initial configuration on $x$, ends in a halted configuration.
For every $i\in\mathbb N$ and $j$ with $0\le j\le r$ such that $j+i=r$, every counter
$c$ with $0\le c\le r+1$, and every augmented configuration $C$ in rewind phase at
$(j,c)$ with empty output and all later blocks blank with their heads at $0$, every
choice word of length exactly $i(T+|x|+2)+1$ causes the amplified machine started from
$C$ to halt.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output probability during rewind]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.rewind_prob}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.rewind_prob}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_const, Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_mono, Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_seg, Randomized.Amplify.ACfg, Randomized.Amplify.Fresh, Randomized.Amplify.RewindAt, Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.finish, Randomized.Amplify.restart, Randomized.Amplify.restart_eq_emb, Randomized.Amplify.rewind_halts, Randomized.Amplify.rewind_last, Randomized.Amplify.rewind_run, Randomized.Amplify.run_halts, Randomized.Amplify.run_prob, Randomized.Amplify.val, Randomized.Amplify.val_zero, Randomized.randProb, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean inputs, let $x$ be an
input, and let $r,T$ be natural numbers. Suppose every length-$T$ choice word makes $N$
halt on $x$ from its initial configuration. For any Boolean value $v$, any $i\in\mathbb
N$, and any $j$ with $0\le j\le r$ and $j+i=r$, take a counter $c$ with $0\le c\le r+1$
and an augmented configuration $C$ in rewind phase at $(j,c)$ with empty output and all
later blocks blank with their heads at $0$. If $c\le j+1$, then the probability that a
uniformly chosen Boolean word of length $i(T+|x|+2)+1$ makes the amplified machine from
$C$ output exactly the one-symbol word $[v]$ equals the probability that, for a
uniformly chosen Boolean word of length $iT$, the decision function applied to $c$ plus
the number of its $i$ consecutive length-$T$ blocks on which $N$ outputs exactly
$[\mathrm{true}]$ equals $v$.
\end{theorem}

Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine with Boolean alphabet, let $r,T$ be natural
numbers, let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $x$ be a
Boolean input word, and let $v$ be a Boolean value. Suppose $N$ halts on $x$ for every
choice word of length exactly $T$. The probability that the amplified machine outputs
the one-symbol word $[v]$ after $T+r(T+|x|+2)+1$ steps equals the probability that, for
a uniformly chosen Boolean word $l$ of length $(r+1)T$, applying $\mathrm{dec}$ to the
number of its $r+1$ consecutive blocks of length $T$ accepted by $N$ gives $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority amplification probability bound]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.majority_randProb_ge}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.majority_randProb_ge}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.acc, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.blockCount_add_not, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_bool_false, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_le_one, Randomized.randProb_mono, Randomized.randProb_not, Randomized.randProb_or_disjoint, Randomized.randProb_tail_le, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a
Boolean input word, and let $T,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy
$0\leq\varepsilon$. If, for some Boolean value $v$, the probability that $N$ outputs the
one-symbol word $[v]$ after $T$ random choice bits is at least $\frac12+\varepsilon$,
then the probability that the majority of $2n+1$ blocks of $T$ choice bits yields $v$ is
at least $1-2(1-4\varepsilon^2)^n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let
$r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and
let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. Suppose there is a natural number $S$ such that, for
every Boolean choice word, the space used by $N$ on that word from its initial
configuration on $x$ is at most $S$. If an amplified configuration $D$ has every
work-tape head within distance $S$ of cell $0$, then for every run index $j<r+1$,

every work-tape head within distance $S$ of cell $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound for the amplified machine]
\lean{Randomized.Amplify.amp_usesSpace}
\label{Randomized.Amplify.amp_usesSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.spaceUsedWith_le_of_ranges, Randomized.Amplify.Good, Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.fresh_init, Randomized.Amplify.good_emb, Randomized.Amplify.init_eq_emb, Randomized.Amplify.reach_comp, Randomized.Amplify.rewindAt_emb, Randomized.Amplify.rewind_good, Randomized.Amplify.step_emb, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape alphabet, let $r$
be a natural number, and let $d:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function.
Suppose $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ bounds the space used by $N$ on every Boolean input
word $x$ and every choice word $w$, when started on $x$. Then, for every such $x$ and
$w$, the space used by the amplified machine on input $x$ under choices $w$ is at most
$(r+1)k(2s(|x|)+1)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $N$.
\end{theorem}
